newsitem.title: CANADA: Court to rule on arbitrager suit June 10.
newsitem.headline: Court to rule on arbitrager suit June 10.

text.p: Manitoba's Court of Queen's Bench was scheduled to rule June 10 on an arbitrager's lawsuit aimed at blocking Canada's second largest grain handler from issuing new shares, United Grain Growers Ltd Chief Executive Officer Brian Hayward said.
"The court hearing and ruling's set for next Tuesday, June 10," Hayward told Reuters.

UGG shares closed on the Toronto Stock Exchange Wednesday at C$14.75 a share after setting a new high of C$16 each last Friday after the firm announced a C$113 million deal with Archer Daniels Midland Co at C$16 a share.

A move by New York arbitrager Oppenheimer & Co to block UGG from issuing new shares should be put to a shareholder vote at the same time as the proposed ADM deal on July 11 that would see UGG issue three million new shares, Hayward said.

"Since one of Oppenheimer's resolutions was to prohibit us from issuing new shares and the ADM deal involves issuing new shares it only made sense to us that both meetings be held at the same time," Hayward said.
Oppenheimer filed a lawsuit in Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench Wednesday to force a vote on June 26 on UGG's poison pill and ability to float new shares.
The legal move came one week after UGG announced the C$113 million deal that would see ADM acquire 45 percent of UGG.
Oppenheimer increased its stake in UGG Tuesday to 1.645 million shares, or 13.16 percent of the 12.5 million limited common voting shares outstanding.

The arbitrager asked on April 28 that shareholders be allowed to vote on removing a massive dilution plan set up by UGG to block a hostile bid by Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators at C$13.75 a share as well as prohibiting UGG from issuing new shares. The Pools own 14.98 percent of UGG.
MPE declined comment, AWP officials were not available.
